cards.explanation: The answer is infants. Paul says he couldn't address them as spiritual, but as worldly, “…as infants in Christ.” I think that's a kind way to say there's growing left to do. And he still opens by calling them “Brothers.”

The answer is False. Paul does not say they're ready for solid food now. He says, “…you are still not ready…” He gave milk then, and he says they're still in that spot. That's not an insult, friends. It's a doctor reading the chart.

The word is jealousy. Paul says, “…there is jealousy and dissension among you…” and that's why he calls them worldly. When people keep score over who has the better leader, jealousy is usually standing right behind them.

The answer is mere men. Paul asks, “are you not mere men?” That's his response to hearing “I follow Paul…” and “I follow Apollos…” I think he's pulling them back down to earth so they can look up again.

The answer is servants. Paul says Apollos and himself are “…servants through whom you believed…” and that the Lord has assigned to each his role. The role came from the Lord, friends. That's a pretty good reason not to brag about it.

The answer is False. Paul planted, Apollos watered, “…but God made it grow.” So Apollos is not the one who made it grow. The growing is God's part, and nobody with a watering can gets to take credit for the harvest.

The answer is True. Paul says the one who plants and the one who waters are “…one in purpose…” They're not rival teams, they're on the same crew. The Corinthians were choosing sides, and Paul says there was only ever one side.

The word is labor. Paul says each “…will be rewarded according to his own labor.” The reward follows the work, not the applause. I've pressed a lot of dough with nobody clapping, and that still counts.
The answer is God's field. Paul says, “you are God’s field, God’s building.” After all that planting and watering, it fits. The Corinthians are the ground God is growing something in.

The word is careful. Paul says, “But each one must be careful how he builds.” The foundation is already set, but what goes on top still matters. Measure twice, friends. I learned that the hard way with a cookie tray and a crooked rack.

The answer is Jesus Christ. Paul says no one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, “…which is Jesus Christ.” Everything else gets built on Him. It's not a team, it's not a favorite preacher. It's Him.

The answer is fire. Paul says the Day will bring each builder's work to light and, “It will be revealed with fire…” Then the fire proves the quality of each man's work. Fire doesn't take opinions, friends. It just shows what's there.
The answer is True. Paul says, “If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.” If the work stands up to the fire, the builder is rewarded. Good work lasts, and Paul says it's noticed.

The answer is False. Paul says if it's burned up, he will suffer loss, but “He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.” So the builder is saved. That's a real loss, and I think it would sting. Still, the builder is saved.

The word is temple. Paul asks, “Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?” That's a big word to give people who were busy arguing. It tells them they're a place where God's Spirit lives.
The word is holy. Paul says, “for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.” That's why he took the warning before it so seriously. What belongs to God is not something to tear down.

The answer is True, and it sounds backwards on purpose. Paul says, “…he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.” He's speaking to anyone who thinks he is wise in this age. I think that's a call to let go of that kind of wisdom first.
The answer is boasting in men. Paul says, “Therefore, stop boasting in men.” That's the whole fight in Corinth, one person bragging about their favorite leader. Paul says to quit it.
The answer is Christ. Paul says, “…and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.” They have everything, and they belong to Him. That's the right way around, friends.
